reflection.assumptions: Pandemic-related changes may have altered clinical work, service delivery, workload, safety concerns, and interactions with patients, requiring health workers to adapt to evolving demands and resource constraints.

Initial Code: Patient perceives traditional medicine as primary treatment  
Clues: "People were having this concept that it won’t be treated by the English way unless I go for traditional native medicines that the only it could be treated." "I was using the traditional way and I saw no improvements that’s when I decided to go to the hospital."  
Initial Code: Patient's access to services is influenced by community referral  
Clues: "I went there, I met with the doctor, the doctor planned it and gave me all the guides how to go about it." "that CHO did you meet him at the hospital or where do you know him? ... we were staying here at the same house."  
Initial Code: Patient acknowledges COVID-19 precautions as necessary  
Clues: "Corona is real and that why the precautions that the government has put in place that the whole world has put in place they said we should abide by them, it real." "they said we should use because when you sneeze it won’t be able to spread so that was all."  
Initial Code: Government measures significantly impact daily life  
Clues: "if these were not put in place like what we are talking here we shouldn’t not have been able to discuss them." "it affected people especially those with asthma diseases the ones with pressure the thing was affecting them."  
Initial Code: School closures lead to negative educational outcomes  
Clues: "look at the results that came out because schools closed earlier then second term school was closed." "there was no studies no caring was there, so that was one of the impacts."  
Initial Code: Transportation issues arise during lockdown  
Clues: "there was no transportation, especially district lockdown transportation was high." "the transport fare from here to Freetown they were asking for le 150,000 can you imagine?"  
Initial Code: Lockdown creates economic strain for daily wage earners  
Clues: "the ones that has no chance you see them sitting down lonely observing and say how, grumbling all over like what is this?" "the ones that are living on daily bread how will they survive so those are the grumbles that we were having."  
Initial Code: Social distancing measures affect community interactions  
Clues: "social distancing is more preventable because of that saliva or the sneezes from someone that it won’t meet with you." "the day when you say lockdown people that has the chance you see them buying things for their homes."

Initial Code: Health worker experiences fear of unknown illness transmission  
Clues: "the increase in number of death. Of cause the death was low but the number of affected people was increasing so that was making everyone scared that you wouldn’t know who has the sick."  
Initial Code: Government enforcement of health measures  
Clues: "they enforced it, they enforced the measures, you don’t abide, and they fine a levy on you."  
Initial Code: Differences in government response between Ebola and COVID-19  
Clues: "during the time of EBOLA their sensitization was if you are sick you call 117... there was no social distancing measures as compared to this now social distance."  
Initial Code: Community adherence to government guidelines due to past experiences  
Clues: "the EBOLA outbreak helped you and your community to prepare for this COVID? exactly."  
Initial Code: Comparison of government communication strategies  
Clues: "the restriction the sensitization was there but during the time of the EBOLA their sensitization was if you are sick you call 117, don’t hide a sick person."  
Initial Code: Health worker reflections on previous public health crises  
Clues: "the EBOLA when it came we had no idea now when the COVID is here the previous government they have already know although they still don’t have measures."  
Initial Code: Public perception of government effectiveness during crises  
Clues: "as this thing break down this government say no let put measures in place now, get experts, all measures put in place so the thing didn’t escalate to that level."  
Initial Code: Government response to COVID-19 rated positively for early action  
Clues: "because they attack the disease earlier." "they give time to the COVID quickly because as we heard it from Europe we had no case here but we had already has a case so immediately when we had that one case government announces it."  
Initial Code: Criticism of inadequate healthcare infrastructure during the pandemic  
Clues: "they were creating centers for admitting people but there was no position so the people who are the victims that were going to those centers were grumbling." "government should try to improve on the health centers, more improvement on the health system especially the drugs."  
Initial Code: Availability of essential drugs as a barrier to healthcare access  
Clues: "certain drugs you need in the hospital, unless they refer you to another facility." "certain drugs that they prescribed for me it wasn’t available."  
Initial Code: Concerns about hospital conditions leading to secondary health issues  
Clues: "if you are not careful you will come out again with another diseases." "if you see behind my back so many rashes I went there and had encounter another sickness then chicken pox had shown on me."  
Initial Code: High costs of healthcare and surgery during the pandemic  
Clues: "I was in doubt because the time when I did this operation for my hernia in 2015 it costs le 500,000 but initially when I went to the finance doctor told me go and pay to that woman, me and the doctor has discussed everything the woman went on writing thinking it was hernia and she wrote le 900,000." "All the drugs are very expensive for this particular operation."  
Initial Code: Comparing quality of care between private and government hospitals  
Clues: "the nurses in the private hospital are more caring, the wards very lonely, very quiet." "they will must come around and asked you if you have your drugs then you ready to administered but if the drugs is not available they will just pass you."  
Initial Code: Emergency care experiences during the pandemic  
Clues: "that in fact was an emergency, I went there under emergency during that time." "I should be out on Monday but I decided to discharge on Sunday."  
Initial Code: Importance of personal relationships with healthcare providers  
Clues: "I wouldn’t want to go and do operation and doctor don’t have acquaintance with me." "I took his number and we have been communicating day and night so I was closed to him before doing the operation."  
Initial Code: Surgical patients feel neglected compared to COVID patients  
Clues: "yes because they are pandemic. They already has it so they should put more premium on them but surgical they should also put premium they should care for us because if they do not care where they do the operation it could reoccur so if you are not careful you will die so they should care for us more."  
Initial Code: Perception of unequal resource allocation  
Clues: "because when the thing has come from international because we see they provide donor for them, they pour more money on COVID but we never saw donor for operation."  
Initial Code: Concern about health worker safety  
Clues: "the health workers have extra besides what they paid them because if catches you, you have risk your life it would transfer so therefore they give them extra charges extra payments from your normal work."  
Initial Code: Need for improved drug availability in hospitals  
Clues: "they should improve on the monitoring not only the buildings like all the facilities more especially the drugs should be available in the hospitals. When you need when they write your prescription you go down and buy quickly and come and go."  
Initial Code: Recommendation for preventive measures during outbreaks  
Clues: "if there is a vaccine that they will inject a person for him not to have that diseases that what they should be fighting for let say an Anti-drug, take the drug and it will be in your system for years."  
Initial Code: Fear of seeking care during the pandemic  
Clues: "people were having other diseases which is not EBOLA but they are afraid to go to the hospital."
